Proposition

↗ prob:2-2

1. ch2:2.12Let $M_1,\ldots ,M_k,N$ be smooth manifolds with or without boundary, with at most one $M_i$ having nonempty boundary. For projections $\pi _i:M_1\times \cdots \times M_k\to M_i$, a map $F:N\to M_1\times \cdots \times M_k$ is smooth if and only if each $F_i=\pi _i\circ F$ is smooth.

Proof

\sketch In product charts, the coordinate representation of $F$ is the tuple of the coordinate representations of the $F_i$. Such a Euclidean map is smooth if and only if each component is smooth.

□
